paragraphs: PURVIS Systems develops, implements, and maintains mission-critical solutions for federal and local governments. Its Fire Station Alerting System automates the process of dispatching fire and rescue personnel, enhancing communications, and decreasing response times. The same page lists engineering services covering the design, development, and modernization of hardware, software, and systems integration.

The clients page names the Department of Defense, the National Institutes of Health, and public safety organizations among those served. Named public safety clients include the Boston Fire Department, the City of Chicago's Office of Emergency Communications, and Charleston County, SC. The alerting system interfaces with computer aided dispatch and radio systems to automate the dispatching of fire and EMS calls in the District of Columbia.

Work for the Department of Defense began with sea trials and sonar experiments aboard the USS Hugh PURVIS in 1973. A partnership with the Fire Department of New York City followed two years later and continues to this day. The about page counts 125+ multi-disciplinary experts on the team.

quote.text: Whether it’s integrating disparate systems, developing tailored software and hardware solutions, providing network engineering services, or implementing life-critical alerting technologies, PURVIS works with you to solve those challenges and right-size solutions for your organization.
